div.head: ECf 35.1 A
div.ab: Fuitque predicta Margareta generosa ualde et optima, scilicet ex parte patris ex nobili genere et sanguine regum Anglorum-Britonum, ex parte uero matris ex genere et sanguine regum Rugorum; sanctissimisque antecessoribus suis in bonis et laudabilibus et insignibus actibus consimilis, preclara effulsit.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 664 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page after ECf 35, 1 as an insertion into ECf retr. 35, 1 (35, 1 A). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 35,1 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
Liebermann prints some words here in smaller type (“ex genere”, “Rugorum”); they are taken over from ECf retr 35 and 35, 1, which his margin names (ECf. retr. 35. 35, 1).

note.seg: ausser Margaretens Heiligkeit weiss der Londoner hier nichts Eigenes; er verficht weibliche Thronfolge: Eleonore von Bretagne, nicht Johann, hätte de iure England erben müssen; der Schottenkönig sei uerus heres ultimi Edwardi; mein Über Leg. Angl. S. 66. 69

apart from Margaret’s sanctity the Londoner knows nothing of his own here; he champions female succession: Eleanor of Brittany, not John, ought de iure to have inherited England; the King of Scots, he says, is uerus heres ultimi Edwardi; my Über Leg. Angl. pp. 66. 69

div.ab: And the aforesaid Margaret was very well born and most excellent, namely on her father's side of noble family and of the blood of the kings of the English-Britons, but on her mother's side of the family and blood of the kings of the Rugians; and, very like her most holy ancestors in good and praiseworthy and distinguished deeds, she shone forth illustrious.
